name: Garrett Motion Inc.

profile.description: Garrett Motion is a global leader in automotive turbocharger and electric-hybrid boosting technology, serving OEM customers across light vehicle, commercial vehicle, and aftermarket segments. The company emerged from Chapter 11 restructuring in 2021 and is investing heavily in E-Turbo (in production with Mercedes-AMG), E-Cooling for battery thermal management, fuel cell compressors, and energy storage solutions as it navigates the ICE-to-electrification transition.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Garrett has successfully emerged from Chapter 11 (2021), stabilized operations, and expanded beyond turbochargers into electrified boosting with the E-Turbo in production with Mercedes-AMG, E-Cooling for battery thermal management, and fuel cell compressors [1][2]. Q1 2026 revenue of $985M (+12% YoY on a reported basis, +6% constant currency) with raised full-year outlook to $3.75B validates the execution [1]. AI Deployment (0/2): Garrett is deploying AI internally for supply chain optimization (o9 Solutions digital planning platform) and risk modeling, but no AI-powered products are shipping to customers and no quantified savings have been disclosed [3]. Market Share (1/2): Garrett is one of two global turbocharger leaders alongside BorgWarner, with a ~50% competitive win rate on available programs and strong demand acceleration in China for both ICE and electrified products [1]. Meaningful player with strong competitive wins but not dominant category-definer. Pipeline (2/2): E-Turbo in production with Mercedes-AMG, E-Cooling and fuel cell components in development with specific OEM timelines, >50% of R&D directed toward new growth technologies, and expanded energy storage cooling partnership provide clear product-revenue visibility [1][2]. R&D Intensity (1/1): Over 50% of R&D spending allocated to new technologies (E-Turbo, E-Cooling, fuel cells) is clearly above the auto parts industry average and reflects strategic commitment to the electrification pivot [1][2].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Garrett's mission 'Advancing Motion' is supported by CEO Rabiller's statement that Garrett 'provides advanced solutions that optimize performance in all vehicles — from high-efficiency turbocharging for ICE, including PHEVs and REEVs, to differentiated electrification technologies supporting the transition to zero-emission mobility' [3]. This is clear about what the company does and connects to the energy transition, but is more of a business positioning statement than a deeply distinctive purpose. Community Impact (0/2): DEI Council established and Global HSE Director hired, but no specific community investment programs, charitable foundations, or dollar-amount philanthropic commitments were identified [3]. Employee Retention (1/2): CEO Olivier Rabiller's 7.67-year tenure provides stability since the 2018 Honeywell spin-off and through the bankruptcy restructuring. Compensation is 87.8% at-risk (equity/bonus), aligning management incentives. However, Glassdoor reviews are mixed (3.6/5) with some citing workplace culture concerns [3]. Insider Buying (0/2): No evidence of meaningful net insider purchases by executives in the last 12 months; Rabiller's significant equity exposure comes from compensation structure rather than open-market buying.

infrastructure.label: STRONG
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as Growth stock. Q1 2026 delivered $985M revenue (+12% YoY reported) with adjusted EBIT of $151M (15.3% margin) and raised 2026 net sales guidance to $3.75B midpoint [1]. Forward P/E of 18.68 is within the 20 target, and PEG ratio of 1.00 is at the Growth target — the key strength of this profile. Profit margin of 9.29% is below the 20% target but improving (from 8.1% a year ago). Revenue growth YoY of 12% is strong but 5yr CAGR of ~2% reflects post-bankruptcy stabilization rather than consistent expansion. D/E scores 0 mechanically due to negative shareholders' equity (-$781M) resulting from the Honeywell spin-off and bankruptcy restructuring [4][5]. ROE is excluded from calculation due to negative equity. Liquidity clears the $1M floor at estimated 800K+ daily volume x $22.20 = ~$17.8M daily dollar liquidity.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (7/9): Garrett manufactures physical turbochargers, E-Turbo systems, and thermal management components — AI structurally cannot replace engineered hardware that operates under extreme temperatures and pressures inside vehicle powertrains [1][2]. The company's engineering data repository, OEM qualification processes, and manufacturing expertise create deep moats against AI substitution. Additionally, AI data center growth increases demand for Garrett's E-Cooling and energy storage thermal management products. Analysts have not flagged AI as a disruption risk for turbocharger manufacturers [5]. AI Opportunity (0/1): Garrett is using AI internally for supply chain optimization and risk modeling but generates no revenue from AI-powered products or services [3].

infinite_game.summary: Garrett is navigating a difficult ICE-to-electrification transition with reasonable discipline — emerging from Chapter 11, directing >50% of R&D to new technologies, and winning production programs for E-Turbo and E-Cooling. The 'Advancing Motion' purpose is credibly articulated, and the company has shown willingness to invest in the electrification future despite current revenue dependence on ICE turbochargers. However, the transformation is still in progress and the Honeywell asbestos litigation legacy adds uncertainty.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (1/3): 'Advancing Motion' connects Garrett's engineering heritage to the energy transition — the company positions its work as enabling cleaner, more efficient transportation across all powertrain types [3]. This is a genuine cause that partially guides strategic decisions (directing >50% of R&D to electrification), but it hasn't been validated through multi-decade consistency since Garrett only became independent in 2018.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): CEO Rabiller's 7.67-year tenure from the Honeywell spin-off through bankruptcy and recovery provides organizational stability [3]. DEI Council established and compensation structure heavily equity-linked (87.8% at-risk). However, Glassdoor reviews at 3.6/5 with some citing workplace culture issues, and the post-bankruptcy environment likely created organizational disruption. Average trust for the industry.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (1/1): Garrett explicitly competes with BorgWarner and acknowledges the competitive pressure drives its innovation investment in electrified boosting and fuel cell technology [1][2]. Management's competitive language focuses on winning programs through better technology rather than destroying competitors — the ~50% win rate is framed as evidence of product quality, not market domination.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Post-bankruptcy emergence in 2021, E-Turbo production with Mercedes-AMG, E-Cooling for EVs, expanded energy storage partnership, and >50% R&D allocation to new technologies represent real strategic evolution from the legacy turbocharger business [1][2]. The company has also settled the Honeywell asbestos indemnity through the restructuring. However, ICE turbochargers still generate the majority of revenue — the transformation is in progress, not complete.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Directing >50% of R&D spending to new growth technologies while the core ICE turbocharger business still generates the majority of revenue demonstrates willingness to invest in the future at some cost to near-term profitability [1][2]. The expanded energy storage cooling partnership shows strategic initiative beyond the auto sector. However, the restructured company has not yet faced a clear test of choosing principle over profit.

investment_thesis: Garrett Motion delivered a breakout Q1 2026 with $985M revenue (+12% YoY reported) and raised its full-year outlook to $3.75B, driven by accelerating demand in China, strong turbocharger win rates (~50% of available programs), and expanding E-Powertrain and energy storage cooling businesses [1]. Adjusted EBIT margin of 15.3% and net profit margin improvement to 9.29% (from 8.1% a year ago) demonstrate operating leverage as the company scales. The PEG ratio of 1.00 and forward P/E of 18.68 offer fair value for a company with multiple growth vectors: E-Turbo in production with Mercedes-AMG, E-Cooling for battery thermal management, and fuel cell components [2]. The Inspire Impact Score of +46 (ALIGNED) with no negative attributions makes GTX one of the cleanest faith-alignment profiles in the auto parts sector.
thesis_continued: The bear case is structural. Negative shareholders' equity (-$781M) from the Honeywell spin-off and bankruptcy restructuring, combined with $1.47B in debt, creates meaningful leverage risk if the auto cycle weakens [4][5]. Revenue growth 5yr CAGR of ~2% reflects post-bankruptcy stabilization rather than sustained expansion, and the long-term ICE-to-EV transition will structurally reduce turbocharger demand over time — Garrett's electrification pivot must succeed to offset this secular headwind. Profit margin of 9.29% is below the target, and the stock has already appreciated 253% over 52 weeks, compressing the margin of safety. The Honeywell asbestos indemnity was addressed in restructuring but remains a reputational overhang. OEM concentration risk and European/Chinese auto cycle cyclicality add volatility [4].
key_catalysts: E-Turbo production ramp with Mercedes-AMG and pipeline of additional OEM programs, with >50% of R&D directed toward new electrification technologies [1][2]
Energy storage cooling partnership expansion opening a non-automotive revenue stream adjacent to the AI data center infrastructure build-out [1]
Continued turbocharger share gains in China and hybrid/PHEV adoption extending the ICE turbocharger runway beyond initial EV transition timelines [1]
key_risks: Negative shareholders' equity (-$781M) and $1.47B debt create amplified downside risk in an auto cycle downturn or credit tightening [4][5]
Long-term ICE-to-EV transition structurally reducing turbocharger demand — electrification pivot must succeed to maintain revenue base [1][2]
253% stock appreciation over 52 weeks has compressed margin of safety; OEM concentration and European/Chinese auto cycle cyclicality add volatility [5]
